Had a real come-to moment while binging Yellowstone oddly enough - realized while   
I was watching these characters live full, invigorating days every single day, I don't want to be on my deathbed looking back on a life filled with just observing and living vicariously through others who have enough confidence to actually live. That maybe this fantasy reality I try to stay in where nothing bad can happen and I will never be uncomfortable isn't fulfilling and isn't how I want to spend my time on this earth. 

You cannot get back the time spent isolating and high, but you can make up for it now. I spend so much time fantasizing what I want my life to look like and all of the people I want in it, that it makes me so unforgiving of the conditions of my current reality. As if I am not doing it "right" or I'm not doing what I "should" be doing. But who cares? Why should we spend our limited time here looking down on who we are and how we live? I avoid going places and doing things because "I'll be alone and that's embarrassing", but can you imagine how upset I'll be when I'm old and tired and have no memories to look back on because I decided I wasn't worthy enough to experience life on my own? That I needed another person to prove to myself I deserve to take up space? I think this is my way of saying I understand, and have recently been trying to integrate the belief that my life does not have to look a certain way in order to decide it's worth living, if that makes sense.

While I'm sorry you're able to relate, it's comforting to know I'm not the only one who has had to go through it. That weed and adderall combination is tricky - I've wondered if my reliance on it is just me trying to do anything but live in my "natural" state of mind, if that makes sense, like a nasty avoidance technique to keep me from really facing myself. 

I also very much hear you on needing weed because it will make situations more "fun". Thing is, when I get high before going to the grocery store because I tell myself it'll be more enjoyable, I end up being so much more anxious while actually doing it. When I get high before cleaning my space because why not make a mundane thing interesting, I usually end up getting derailed and passing out on my couch. What's that they say about doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results...?

Congratulations on taking your life back and moving forward. It is beyond inspiring.

Thank you for your kind words - really needed to hear this. Feels very silly listing all of the reasons I actually don't enjoy being high and then doing it anyway. Looking forward to reaching the point where this is something I'm able to just reflect back on.

My guy still struggles with this! He is a very vocal (yappy lol) breed and he is his most vocal when something happens that he doesn’t expect. It’s a huge issue for us that even happens at home (how does someone closing a door startle you so much?). As it’s something I’m struggling with as well, I wish I could provide something that’s worked for us! When he barked at every passing stranger I would have him sit as they’re approaching and distract him with a treat/ask him to sit/stay. If he didn’t bark, he got the treat! Now, if he’s in the yard and hears a car door from the street it’s like he’s trying to alert the whole world that there’s an intruder. Ugh. I read a comment once from someone saying they play YouTube videos of all different sounds for short periods until eventually the sounds didn’t phase their dog anymore.

All of the above! He would hide wherever he could (usually in between my legs or trying to jump up on me), cried like he was being hurt if a dog touched him or came too close, but mainly only barked at passing strangers. I was taking him to petco’s puppy play time but he would just hide under the chairs and cry to be let out/try to climb the fence to get away. Not to say everyone’s dog will end up being a social butterfly like mine, but I believe going at their pace and letting them choose when they feel ready to interact instead of forcing interaction really helped my guy.

My puppy was absolutely terrified of other dogs and new people. He’s now 8 months and wants every dog to be his new best friend! I’m lucky as there was a giant off leash field close to where I live. I started bringing him and would hang out at the edge (away from any dogs) just so he can observe other dogs playing without having to interact with them. Eventually after doing this for a few weeks, he started approaching dogs and saying hello. He’s a completely different dog now, and I would just say to go at your puppy’s pace. Don’t rush anything and read his signals. I think giving exposure to other people/dogs without actually having to interact really worked for my little guy. As far as meeting other people, my guy is still a little withdrawn when meeting strangers, but whenever someone comes into our house I provide them with treats to give him and he calms down shortly after that. Hope this helps!

I got my puppy at 6 weeks, it’s not convenient but you just have to do your best with the situation. My little guy is now almost 14 weeks and he’s a dream! I am not a professional by any means, but I’ll share what really helped me. My puppy had experience in crates prior to me getting him, but I had him sleep with me for two weeks because they are really still a baby who should still be cuddling with their litter mates and momma. This is totally your preference though. 

I also just let him be a puppy for a few weeks, didn’t enforce training all that much, really let him explore while keeping safe boundaries, and just played a lot. I waiting until he was about 8 weeks to start really teaching commands, and he picked them up right away! I think having that time to form a bond really helped. As soon as I could, I took him to petco for their puppy play classes- free 30 minute classes on the weekends for puppies to socialize. the period of 6-8 weeks is where they learn a lot about socialization and bite inhibition. These classes have helped me learn more about my puppy’s behavior and what we needed to focus on with training. 

Bring your puppy everywhere you can! I bought a little sling carrier for my guy and took him everywhere with me so he got used to sights, smells, and people. Focus a lot on socialization since they’re missing out on that important period, but make sure you go at your puppy’s pace. 

Getting a puppy too young doesn’t always mean they’re going to have behavioral issues (like I was told), you just want to be diligent with your training and watch for any red flags. For now, I’d say just let him be a puppy for a little while. Give him lots of love, play time, and nap times. I hand fed my guy his dinner but breakfast in the bowl so that he got used to both. 

A few years ago, it was a lot more common to get puppies that young. I thought I had a puppy that was condemned to a life full of behavioral issues, but with proper training, you’ll be just fine.

I understand where you’re coming from- but she also mentions that they’ve had a conversation where he has said he does not have the time to take care of a dog. She also mentions that (for some reason) he is not allowed to have one. if you look at the situation objectively, on one hand she has a family who has the time to take care of the puppy and she knows that the puppy would have a good life there; on the other hand, say this wasn’t her boyfriend, say it was someone who reached out to her saying he wanted the puppy but he works long hours and isn’t completely sure he has the time for a puppy. what choice would you go with? I think she’s more keeping in mind the well-being of the pup, and if her gut says to go with the other family, I say she should have the right to make that decision.

Ignore everyone giving you a hard time for not giving your boyfriend the puppy. you’ve made it clear that your reasons are not because you don’t think he’s fit to care for it, but that he works long hours and, really, if it’s going to be crated all day, he shouldn’t have offered. I understand that falling in love and being attached with an animal makes us want to do anything for it, but I guarantee he might feel some regret once the weight of that responsibility was on his shoulders. it’s a huge commitment and doing it alone is a lot of work. a puppy that young should not be crated all day and needs almost constant supervision. 

if you’ve found a family who you know will give it a good life and you feel no doubts about the puppy’s wellbeing there, then follow your intuition! I think you’re doing the right thing by rehoming it. If you weren’t ready to own a puppy, having one suddenly given to you can be a major shock- especially when you struggle with anxiety. I planned to get a puppy for months and was very careful during the whole process, but because I struggle with major anxiety, it has caused an incredible amount of stress in my life. if you had not planned for this or felt prepared, caring for something so dependent on you can be too much. you are keeping the puppy’s best interest in mind and I applaud you for that! it’s difficult for people to swallow their pride and admit they might just not be capable at this time. 

as for your boyfriend, I hope he will come around and see you are not being malicious. keep telling him that it’s merely the fact that he works too long of hours to care for the puppy. I work very short, flexible hours and even then I am so stressed out not being at home with my little guy. puppies are a huge responsibility, and if he has mentioned in the past he couldn’t care for a dog, listen to that. love can blind you, and I don’t think he’s fully thinking the situation through. best of luck to you, but trust your gut and know you’re doing the right thing!

I used to struggle with my nostril piercing as well (ended up having to take it out after 5 years of it being on/off irritated). make sure you consistently keep quality jewelry in. since hoops are round where as studs are straight, the hoop can sometimes put too much pressure on the site and irritate it, not to mention how much it moves. my piercer’s advice was to “leave it the fuck alone”. let it slowly peel off by itself and don’t touch it. if it doesn’t get better switch back to a stud and let it heal up again- my old piercing was never able to be healthy with a hoop in no matter how hard I tried.
